title: Railboard: compact capacity briefing and manual throttle affordances
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Design a compact, operator-focused capacity briefing (Railboard) for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health, cost, and manual throttle controls in a single concise strip. The Railboard will be intended for on-call operators and SREs who need quick situational awareness and low-friction intervention controls during congestion or degraded performance. It sits at the top of the pool detail page and is optimized for single-row scan while expanding into lightweight panels for deeper controls.

Goals:
- Provide an at-a-glance health strip: recent SLO trend sparkline, token-cost delta, active queue length indicator, and node-level thermal flag.
- Add a manual throttle affordance: a safe, discoverable slider + quick-presets (25/50/75%) to reduce token concurrency for low-latency critical routes. Include cooldown/hysteresis visualization and confirmation flow to avoid accidental impact.
- Surface a surge-preview simulation: a transient sandbox that shows estimated latency and cost impact of applying throttles or burst allowances, using historical workload samples.
- Keep keyboard and screen-reader accessibility; minimal client JS interactions.
- Ensure the Railboard works in Dedicated and Private deployments; feature gates for Dedicated-only policies (e.g., reserved capacity interactions).

Scope: top-row compressed UI, expandable micro-panels (health details, throttle controls, surge preview), tooltip-driven explanations, and an initial prototype for user testing with SREs and two enterprise customers. Not in scope: full rollout automation flows, persistent policy authoring (handled in separate policy editor ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Compact strip appears at top of pool detail and matches provided spec with <= 3 lines of vertical height when collapsed
Sparkline shows last 60 minutes with hover-to-highlight and point-of-interest markers for SLO breaches
Throttle slider applies local UI constraints and opens a confirmation modal that lists affected routes and estimated latency/cost impact
Surge-preview simulation uses last-24h trace sample and renders a side-by-side 'before/after' cost+latency estimate
Keyboard operable and aria labels implemented for all controls; tested with NVDA or VoiceOver
Design handoff includes Figma screens, token/spacing scale, and component states for 'healthy', 'degraded', 'congested', and 'critical'
decisions: Keep collapsed height to 3 lines to minimize vertical real estate and prioritize scanability
Throttle control performs optimistic UI update with a backend guard that can auto-revert if policy conflict detected
Surge-preview will be read-only and run in a sandbox; it will not apply changes without explicit confirmation
No persistent policy storage in this ticket; the Railboard only issues ephemeral manual overrides (TTL-based)
risks: Operators may overuse manual throttles leading to degraded throughput for non-critical work
Estimations in surge-preview could be misinterpreted; need clear confidence bands and provenance info
Private deployments with strict network egress may not be able to run simulation jobs; provide server-side fallbacks
user_research_notes: Sprint 1 usability test (3 SREs): all participants found the sparkline useful; one requested node-level roll-up toggles
Customer session (Enterprise A): asked for a 'safe mode' toggle that only allows reductions, not increases, to prevent accidental capacity expansion
Accessibility pass found missing focus outline on slider; resolved in v2 mockups
